info.title: Campaign Assistant API
info.summary: Campaign drafting over a shared, runtime-validated contract.
info.description:
Every endpoint below is described by the shared contract package: the request and response schemas served here are the ones the web app validates against at runtime.

Authentication is a bearer access token obtained from `auth.signIn`. Errors are always an RFC 9457 problem document. Chat replies can be streamed as server-sent events; see `chat.messages.stream`.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Verifies the credentials, then mints an access/refresh pair. Refresh tokens are single-use: `auth.refresh` rotates them, so a token can only be exchanged once.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new session
post.description: Rotates the pair. The presented refresh token is revoked as part of the exchange, so replaying it is rejected as `session_expired`.
Revokes the refresh token presented in the body. Idempotent: signing out twice is not an error. The access token stays usable until it expires, which keeps sign-out instantaneous.

get.description: Paginated and filterable. Filtering, sorting and pagination all happen server-side, so a page never depends on how large the table is.

post.description: Adds one customer. A duplicate email is rejected with `conflict` rather than merged, so the caller decides what to do with it.

get.description: Aggregate totals for the dashboard: headcount, active customers, lifetime value and average value.

post.description: Partial import: valid rows are persisted and invalid ones are reported per row, so one bad line does not fail the whole file. `row` is the 1-based position within `customers`.

get.description: Distinct countries present in the customer base, sorted alphabetically.
Total spend per country, ordered by amount so a dashboard can render a ranking without sorting client-side.
Returns saved segments with their stored conditions and last known audience size.

post.description: Conditions are combined with AND. Clauses keep the order they were written in so a saved segment stays readable.

delete.description: Removes the segment. Campaigns generated from it keep their stored copy of the segment name, so history stays readable.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the resource being addressed.

post.description: Counts the customers matching unsaved conditions. Use it while building, before committing a segment.
Runs the configured language model over a saved segment and returns a drafted campaign. Generation is a server concern: the browser never talks to the model provider.

patch.description: Legal transitions are `draft` to `ready` to `sent`, plus `ready` back to `draft`. Anything else is rejected with `conflict`.

post.description: Non-streaming counterpart of `chat.messages.stream`: one request, one complete assistant message.

post.summary: Send a message and stream the reply
post.description: Server-sent events. Frames are `start`, then one `delta` per chunk, then a terminal `done` or `error`. The request stays open for the whole reply, so a proxy in front of the API must not buffer it.
